title: Stage 1: Fake backends
summary: Stand up the systems the platform will integrate: a catalogue, a warehouse and an order system, each with failures you can trigger on demand.

steps.title: The platform you will build
body: Over eight stages you build Acme Books' integration platform in **one** ASP.NET Core program, in three layers:
```text
consumer ──► /gateway + middleware ──► /api/... integration ──► /backend/... systems
token, scope, limit        route, transform,        catalogue, warehouse,
log, product, metrics      validate, errors, retry  orders (fakes)
In real life these are separate deployments; here they share one process so the tests can drive all of them,
but the integration still calls the backends **over real HTTP**, exactly as it would across a network.
**Stage 1** builds the backends. They are deliberately *not* what consumers should see: different field names,
an internal field, an internal header, and **magic inputs that fail on demand**, so every error path can be tested.

steps.title: Stage 1 spec
body: Seed three books (`isbn`, `title`, `authorFirst`, `authorLast`, `priceCents`, `internalCost`, stock):
| ISBN | Title | Author | priceCents | internalCost | stock |
| `9780134757599` | Refactoring | Martin Fowler | 4499 | 1800 | 12 |
| `9780131103627` | The C Programming Language | Brian Kernighan | 3999 | 1500 | 0 |
| `9781492056355` | Fluent Python | Luciano Ramalho | 5299 | 2100 | 3 |
- `GET /backend/books/{isbn}` → `200 {"isbn","title","authorFirst","authorLast","priceCents","internalCost"}` and the header
`X-Backend-Node: catalogue-db-3` on every answer. Unknown → `404 {"error":"no such row"}`.
Magic: `9780000000500` → `500 {"error":"NullReferenceException at PriceRules.cs:42"}`;
`9780000000504` → waits 5 s (`Task.Delay(5000, ctx.RequestAborted)`, catching the cancellation) then `200`;
`9780000000999` → `200` with an HTML body (`text/html`).
- `GET /backend/stock/{isbn}` → `{"sku","onHand"}` (the warehouse's names). Unknown → `404`.
- `POST /backend/orders` with `{"isbn","quantity","email"}` → `201 {"orderNo":"ORD-1",...}`, numbering 1, 2, 3...
- Every backend call is remembered: `GET /backend/requests` → `[{"method","path","headers":{...}}]`, so tests can see exactly what each backend **received**.
- `GET /health` → `{"status":"up"}`.

steps.prompt: Why give the fake backends magic inputs like `9780000000504` that always take 5 seconds?
options: So the integration's timeout and error mapping can be tested deterministically, on every run
To slow the tests down realistically
To test the gateway's rate limit
steps.explain: If failures only happen in production, your error handling ships untested. Make every failure a test input.
